Beijing is an ancient capital in northern China. Its long history goes back more than three thousand years. Today about twenty-one million people live in the city region. Guidebooks say that the pace of life in Beijing is very fast: people hurry between skyscrapers, ring roads fill with cars at rush hour, and meetings often start on time. Citizens are proud of their culture—the Temple of Heaven, the Forbidden City, and of course famous Beijing roast duck on a family dinner table. When we compare two cities, we use comparative adjectives such as faster, busier, or older to describe polite differences.
Beijing is busier than Chengdu.
Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou are all big cities. Shanghai is one of the busiest cities in China.
Boss traps: farther versus further, older versus elder, latest versus last.
Both Beijing and Chengdu have a recorded history of more than three thousand years.
But we can say: one of the most exciting lessons of the term.
Chengdu hotpot tastes spicier than Beijing duck.

Chengdu is a lively city in southwest China. It also has a recorded history of more than three thousand years. Like Beijing, the population is about twenty-one million. However, many travel writers say that daily life in Chengdu feels slower and more relaxing: teahouses stay noisy until late at night, parks fill with chess players, and friends enjoy long spicy hotpot dinners. Chengdu is famous for giant pandas that attract families from around the world. Students sometimes joke that Chengdu hotpot tastes spicier than Beijing duck—let us check that idea with careful English.
Chengdu is more famous for pandas than many small towns .
Chengdu is more relaxing than Beijing.
China is one of the greatest countries in the world.

Lisa joined two clubs this term. She thinks playing basketball is more exciting than swimming because her team practices harder every week. Her elder sister prefers reading; she spends more time in the library than Lisa does. Their math teacher says the mid-term exam was more difficult than the quizzes, but careful students did better. Lisa hopes next month's speech contest will be less stressful than the exam.

Many people say that living in the countryside is quieter than living downtown. However, city parks today are becoming cleaner and more colorful than before. Scientists believe that if we plant more trees, the air will be fresher and people may feel healthier. Some experts also think walking is safer than driving short distances when the roads are busy. In the future, cities might use more solar energy, which could be cheaper than coal in some areas.

Remember: good and well become better and best. Bad and ill become worse and worst. Use farther for physical distance and further for abstract meaning. Use older with than, but elder only before a noun like elder brother. Latest means most recent; last means final in a sequence.
